core.title: Report verb-object naming drift across the existing capability/feature corpus without blocking
core.given: A CONFIRM-phase run with product capability and feature artifacts already on disk, whatever their history or conformance
core.when: The corpus naming check scans those on-disk names, or the planner reads its drift report
core.then: Report every non-conforming capability/feature name (artifact kind, slug, reason) with a total count, as advisory only — never block on it.
prefer: Treat the count as the signal: a rising count means new drift entered outside the authoring gate — the only actionable part; a falling count means debt was paid opportunistically.
avoid: Widening the naming lexicon to clear the report — it silences a rule that correctly describes the corpus.
Turning the report into a blocking gate or failing a plan because the count is non-zero.
core.why: The authoring-time naming gates read only the plan session's kept units, so hand-renamed or out-of-session artifacts drift unnoticed; the count makes the drift visible. The report stays advisory because renaming a named unit is unaffordable, and a blocking rule with no affordable remedy gets ignored.
evidence: The corpus check output lists each non-conforming capability/feature with artifact kind, slug and reason, plus a total count (also reported when zero).
The check runs with advisory enforcement (severity 2): non-conforming names never fail the run.
The naming lexicon was not widened to lower the count; a rise versus the previous count is surfaced as new out-of-gate drift.
verification: A naming-pattern check that runs on every confirm-phase (CONFIRM) run and scans the product capability and feature names already on disk — the on-disk corpus, not the plan session's kept units. How that corpus is enumerated is the checker's own detail, deferred to the realization; no profile value is required for it.
Each finding reports the artifact kind, the slug (name) and the reason; the total count is reported even when it is zero.

Disposition is advisory, severity 2, and load-bearing by design: the check reports with a count and never blocks, never fails a run. Per-rule severity and disposition belong to the rule (core verification), not to the profile.

The check does not cover the authoring path: naming a new product capability or feature inside a plan session is gated by the authoring-time naming rules, and anything authored through a plan session conforms by construction — this rule is the corpus half, catching only hand-renamed or out-of-session artifacts.
Typical non-conformance reasons reported: the name leads with a noun; the name carries an 'and' connective; rarely, the leading verb is genuinely missing from the naming lexicon.

Count semantics: the count is the artefact — a rise versus the previous count is surfaced as new drift that entered outside the authoring gate (the only actionable signal); a fall means debt was paid opportunistically while the artifact was already being touched for other reasons.

fires: Every CONFIRM run: scan the existing product capability and feature names on disk and report the non-conforming count, including when the count is zero and when every artifact was authored through the plan session.

Interpreting a drift report (separate from running the check): the planner reads the count and decides whether a rise signals new out-of-gate drift, or is tempted to widen the naming lexicon or block on a non-zero count.
doesNotFire: Naming a new product capability or feature inside a plan session — that authoring path is gated by the authoring-time naming rules, not by this report.

bunOnly.text: planner.capability.name-is-verb-object and planner.feature.name-is-verb-object gate the authoring path (confirm_naming reads session.kept_units(), so anything authored through atdd plan conforms by construction); neither looks at the corpus.

bunOnly.text: Rename cost (why non-blocking): a name is carried by the directory, the product capability URN, every feature/DESIRED_OUTCOME/acceptance URN beneath it, test filenames, component URNs in code headers, both registries and the State Store bindings — renaming one product capability touches roughly 54 files, 37 of them tests.
bunOnly.reason: A measured, stack-specific inventory of what carries a name (DESIRED_OUTCOME/acceptance URNs, State Store bindings, registries, 54/37 file counts); the core keeps only the neutral conclusion 'renaming is unaffordable'.

neutralityNotes: 'product capability' and 'feature' are retained in the core because they are the closed profile vocabulary's shared structure terms (layout.capability_dir, layout.feature_dir, urn.capability, urn.feature), not Bun-specific names; a stack with different local names supplies them through those profile keys. 'CONFIRM' is the shared plan-workflow phase name, kept in activation facts and given. The verb-object conformance predicate and its lexicon are owned by the companion authoring-time naming rules, so the core references them generically and the concrete rule ids stay bunOnly (verifier_detail[3]); no vocabulary key is needed for the lexicon. Per-rule severity and disposition are not profile keys: the rule's assigned severity 2 and the advisory disposition are retained in core:verification (and evidence[1]) as the vocabulary's notProfileKeys require. bun.json states no capability/feature directory patterns and no scan roots, so no layout or roots profile requirement is extracted; the core keeps the corpus scope ('product capability and feature names already on disk') and defers the exact enumeration of that corpus to the realization's checker, recorded in core:verification — no directory values were invented. Both activation facts need new observers (the phase and the on-disk corpus are not currently observable facts).
